cards.b: A conductor moving across a magnetic field, or a changing field linking with a conductor, induces an e.m.f. across the conductor.

cards.f: Three ways to increase induced e.m.f.
cards.b: Move faster (faster change of field), use a stronger magnet, use more turns on the coil.
No relative movement or no change in the field (e.g. magnet held still in the coil), or a wire moving parallel to the field lines.

cards.f: Why does an induced e.m.f. reverse when you pull the magnet out?
cards.b: The change in field is reversed, so the e.m.f. reverses direction.
Coil rotating in a magnetic field; its sides cut field lines and induce an alternating e.m.f.

cards.f: Role of slip rings and brushes in a generator
cards.b: Each end of the coil has its own ring; brushes press on them to connect the rotating coil to the external circuit.

cards.f: Coil position for zero e.m.f. in a generator
cards.b: Plane perpendicular to the field: sides move parallel to the field lines, not cutting them.
Plane parallel to the field: sides cut field lines fastest.

cards.f: Rotating generator faster: effect on graph
cards.b: Higher peaks and a higher frequency (peaks closer together, shorter period).
Two insulated coils (primary and secondary) wound on a soft-iron core.
Step-up: more turns on secondary, Vs > Vp. Step-down: fewer turns on secondary, Vs < Vp.
P = I²R. Halving the current cuts the loss to a quarter.

cards.f: Why transmit electricity at high voltage?
cards.b: Same power P = IV with a smaller current, so much less power wasted as heat in the cables (I²R); thinner cables possible.

gaps.s: A transformer with a soft-iron core has a primary coil and a ___ coil.
A transformer with more turns on the secondary than the primary is a ___ transformer.
A transformer has 100 primary turns and 500 secondary turns. With 12 V input, the output is ___ V.
A 100% efficient transformer steps 20 V up to 200 V. The current in the secondary is ___ times smaller than in the primary.
The power lost as heat in a cable of resistance R carrying current I is P = ___ R.
The e.m.f. in an a.c. generator is zero when the coil is ___ to the field.
Power stations typically generate at about 25 kV, then a ___ transformer raises the voltage.

short.q: State three factors that increase the e.m.f. induced when a magnet is moved into a coil.
short.model: Faster movement of the magnet, a stronger magnet, more turns on the coil.

short.q: A transformer has 200 turns on its primary and 50 turns on its secondary. The input is 240 V. Calculate the output voltage and state the type of transformer.
short.model: Vs = 240 × 50 ÷ 200 = 60 V. It is a step-down transformer.

short.q: A 100% efficient transformer has a primary of 230 V and 2.0 A, and a secondary of 23 V. Calculate the secondary current.
Explain why electricity is transmitted at very high voltage.
short.model: For a given power, higher voltage means a smaller current (P = IV). Power loss in cables is I²R, so a smaller current wastes much less energy as heat.
points: P = IV so higher V gives lower I

short.q: Sketch-describe the e.m.f. against time graph of a simple a.c. generator and state how it changes if the coil is rotated faster.
short.model: A smooth repeating wave alternating between positive and negative peaks, one cycle per revolution. Faster rotation gives higher peaks and a shorter period (higher frequency).
